blocks.content: Squire is a personal note-taking app built from Notion-style blocks. Poke around, edit anything, and see how it works.

- [[Blocks and Formatting]]: text, tables, checklists, columns
- [[Variables and Widgets]]: variables, formulas, and interactive widgets
- [[Linking Notes]]: links between notes
- [[About Scripts]]: Python that reads and edits the notebook

- [ ] Click into a block and type
- [ ] Right-click a note in the sidebar
- [ ] Press **Ctrl+P** and jump to a note by name
- [ ] Click the calendar button on the far left for a daily note
Notes are plain JSON files, one per note, kept in a single notebook folder.

Squire runs from a single Docker image (amd64 and arm64, so PCs, Raspberry Pis and Apple Silicon all work). Your notes are plain files in a folder you choose, and updating the image never touches them.

```yaml
services:
  squire:
    image: ghcr.io/jackharris2215/squire:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "8765:8765"
    environment:
      - SQUIRE_PASSWORD=changeme   # the password the app asks for
    volumes:
      - ./notebook:/data/notebook  # your notes live here
```
Then run `docker compose up -d` and open http://localhost:8765. To update later: `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`.
Always set `SQUIRE_PASSWORD`, and don't expose the port to the internet. Use a version tag like `:1.0.0` instead of `:latest` to stay on one release.
